findings.title: Secret written directly in the code
findings.description: A password, API key or signing secret appears as a literal string in a source file.
findings.impact: Anyone who sees the code (backups, sharing, version control) gets the secret, and it cannot be rotated without changing code.
findings.evidence: password is assigned a literal value (not-…, 21 characters)

remediation.summary: Move the secret to the environment and read it through config.
steps: Delete the literal from the code.
Add a variable to .env (and a placeholder to .env.example).
Read it via the typed config object.
Rotate the exposed secret, since it must be considered leaked.

verification.howToConfirmFixed: The secrets scan and static scan report nothing; the old secret has been revoked.

triage.reason: Deliberately wrong or weak passwords that the runtime probes send to the app under test to check it refuses them. They are not credentials for anything.
triage.by: Claude (AI-assisted review) — pending confirmation by a human maintainer

findings.title: Route registered without defineRoute
findings.description: A route is added with app.get / router.post directly instead of defineRoute.
findings.impact: The route skips the registry's mandatory authorization declaration, validation, CSRF and rate-limit defaults, so it may be reachable by anyone.
findings.evidence: router.get('/projects/:id/report-runs') is not registered through defineRoute()

remediation.summary: Register every route through defineRoute with an explicit auth value.
steps: Replace router.<method>(path, handler) with defineRoute(router, { method, path, auth, schema }, handler).
Add the route to routes.manifest.json.
remediation.example: defineRoute(router, { method: 'GET', path: '/notes/:id', auth: 'user', owner: { entity: 'note', param: 'id' }, schema: { params: IdParams } }, handler);

verification.howToConfirmFixed: The startup check assertAllRoutesRegistered passes; dast.authz.unregistered-route passes.

triage.reason: The route registry is a convention of generated apps. SecureVibe mounts its whole API under /api behind requireSession, csrfCheck and requireJsonBody (server/src/app.ts), after the global host allow-list, origin check and rate limit.
triage.by: Claude (AI-assisted review) — pending confirmation by a human maintainer

findings.title: File read or written at a user-controlled path

location.snippet: if (!existsSync(appDir)) throw notFound('This project has not been built yet.');

findings.description: A node:fs call receives a path that includes request data.

findings.title: File path built from user input
findings.description: path.join or path.resolve is called with a value from a request.
findings.impact: A value like ../../.env lets a user read or write files outside the intended folder, including secrets.
findings.evidence: join(... appDir)

remediation.summary: Look files up by internal id and never use user text in a path.
steps: Store files under random ids (the uploads module does this).
Resolve the path from the database record, not from the request.
If a name must be used, allow only [a-z0-9-] and verify the resolved path starts with the base directory.
remediation.example:
const upload = await uploads.getOwned(req.user, req.valid.params.id);
const filePath = path.join(config.dataDir, 'uploads', upload.id); // id is a uuid from the DB

verification.howToConfirmFixed: dast.input.path-traversal-smoke passes; the static scan reports nothing.

triage.reason: appDir comes from ProjectStore.paths(), which validates the project id; the joined names are fixed strings.
triage.by: Claude (AI-assisted review) — pending confirmation by a human maintainer

findings.description: A JSON body containing __proto__ or constructor.prototype keys was accepted.
findings.impact: Crafted input may alter the behaviour of all objects in the process, bypassing checks or crashing the app.

findings.title: fetch() used outside the HTTP client

location.snippet: const res = await fetch('https://registry.npmjs.org/', { method: 'HEAD', signal: controller.signal });

findings.description: Code calls the global fetch directly instead of outboundFetch from src/lib/http-client.ts.
findings.impact: The call bypasses the outbound allow-list, timeouts, size cap and redirect control, so a user-influenced address could reach internal services (server-side request forgery).
findings.evidence: Line 59 of server/src/api/preflight.ts: const res = await fetch('https://registry.npmjs.org/', { method: 'HEAD', signal: controller.signal });

remediation.summary: Use outboundFetch and add the host to OUTBOUND_ALLOWED_HOSTS.
steps: Import outboundFetch.
Add the destination host to OUTBOUND_ALLOWED_HOSTS in .env and .env.example.
Never build the URL from user input.
remediation.example:
import { outboundFetch } from '../../lib/http-client.ts';
const res = await outboundFetch('https://api.weather.example/today?city=' + encodeURIComponent(city));

verification.howToConfirmFixed: Search for 'fetch(' outside src/lib/http-client.ts and confirm no matches.

triage.reason: The shared http-client is a convention of generated apps. SecureVibe's server makes one outbound request of its own (a HEAD to registry.npmjs.org during preflight) besides the Anthropic SDK; the web UI only calls its own origin with same-origin credentials.
triage.by: Claude (AI-assisted review) — pending confirmation by a human maintainer

remediation.summary: Keep ignore-scripts=true and prefer packages without install scripts.
steps: Confirm .npmrc has ignore-scripts=true.
If the package needs its script, replace it with an alternative that does not.

verification.howToConfirmFixed: config.ignore-scripts passes; the package is removed or accepted with a note.
